estimates.outcome: Unique idea concepts within each condition (cosine-similarity threshold 0.8)
estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: Number of unique idea concepts divided by the total ideas in the condition. Google Universal Sentence Encoder embeddings; ideas overlap when their cosine similarity exceeds 0.8. Computed across different participants’ submissions within each arm. One aggregate value per condition. Main measure identified on PDF pp. 1-2 (printed pp. 1107-1108).

sources.quote: The error bars show 95% confidence intervals for individual proportions.

estimates.notes: The primary measure for Experiment 1. The local PDF reports arm values only as bar labels in Fig. 1; they are left null under extraction-spec rule 1 on figure-only numbers. Error bars are individual-arm confidence intervals; their numerical endpoints are not printed. ci_level records the caption’s confidence level for both arm proportions, not an interval for a contrast. No difference, exact p-value, test statistic, SD or SE is printed in the local PDF. Supplementary Table 1 contains the numerical comparisons but could not be inspected. The uncertainty calculation and its sampling unit therefore remain unverified. No arithmetic contrasts were derived. The reanalysis says each participant submitted one idea, whereas the original Methods allowed multiple ideas in one submission (c010 PDF p. 6, printed p. 1911). How those submissions were embedded cannot be checked from this PDF.

estimates.outcome: Number of ideas containing the word 'sprinkler'
estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: Raw count of ideas containing the word 'sprinkler' within the entire condition pool; a descriptive keyword measure of conceptual convergence across participants. The *_mean fields store the printed arm-level counts, not participant-level means or percentages. The aggregation unit is a set of outputs.

sources.locator: PDF p. 1 (printed p. 1107), right column, first paragraph, Experiment 2A
sources.quote: Indeed, in Lee and Chung’s experiment 2A, 20 out of 96 ChatGPT-aided ideas included the word ‘sprinkler’, as opposed to only 7 in the web-search-aided condition and 12 in the human-only condition.

estimates.notes: Descriptive full-arm comparison with no inferential test or uncertainty. The treatment denominator printed in the quote is an idea count, so it is not entered as a participant count. Neither comparison-arm denominator is printed in the local PDF. No proportions or count differences are computed. Larger counts indicate more convergence on this particular concept, but do not by themselves adjust for differing arm sizes. The form codes the unit as output; set is used here because the reported values count occurrences across the entire arm pool.

sources.locator: PDF p. 2 (printed p. 1108), right column, first paragraph, Experiment 2b
sources.quote: In the extreme case of study 2b (suggesting a toy for a seven-year-old child using a brick and a fan), only 6% of the AI-generated ideas (ChatGPT-only) were unique, compared with 100% of human ideas.

estimates.notes: The primary measure for Experiment 2b. The local PDF reports arm values only as bar labels in Fig. 1; they are left null under extraction-spec rule 1 on figure-only numbers. Error bars are individual-arm confidence intervals; their numerical endpoints are not printed. ci_level records the caption’s confidence level for both arm proportions, not an interval for a contrast. No difference, exact p-value, test statistic, SD or SE is printed in the local PDF. Supplementary Table 1 contains the numerical comparisons but could not be inspected. The uncertainty calculation and its sampling unit therefore remain unverified. No arithmetic contrasts were derived. Exception to the missing arm levels: the body text explicitly reports the shared Human-only pool as 100% unique, so control_mean is 100 in percentage units. The assisted-human treatment value remains null. The AI-only percentage in the same sentence is excluded because no person worked in that arm.

open_items: Obtain and inspect the separate Supplementary Information at https://static-content.springer.com/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41562-025-02173-x/MediaObjects/41562_2025_2173_MOESM1_ESM.pdf. It is not embedded in the local PDF. The publisher URL and https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/zf3s2/files/osfstorage/ were requested with Python urllib and User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1; both failed with WinError 10013 (socket access forbidden). No local copy was found in the paper library, project, designated data directory, downloads or accessible temporary directories.

Primary unique-fraction point estimates appear only in Fig. 1 of the available source. They were left null under the figure-only rule, apart from the Human-only percentage explicitly printed in the Experiment 2b body text. The individual-arm interval endpoints are also not printed. Supplementary Table 1 is needed to fill arm levels and contrast uncertainty without reading values from the figure.

All alternate thresholds and alternative similarity/tree metrics require the separate supplement. The omitted-outcome list records them separately for each experiment. The main-text tally of significant comparisons is not an effect estimate and does not supply their exact p-values.

Confirm the people actually analyzed in each diversity comparison. Main-text counts of ideas are not entered as participant counts; screening-form supplement counts and data-audit counts were not independently verifiable in the available PDF. Study randomized counts and analyzed counts remain null. Original-paper counts are not assumed to be reanalysis counts.
The reported keyword counts lack comparison-arm denominators and uncertainty; counts alone cannot provide a rate comparison adjusted for differing pool sizes.

Verify the treatment of multiple-idea submissions in Experiment 1. The reanalysis’s one-idea statement conflicts with the original experiment’s permission to enter multiple ideas; the posted code/data could not be inspected.

Verify how uncertainty accounts for the shared observations in diversity statistics and whether the supplement’s interval correction matches the main caption’s claim of Bonferroni-corrected difference intervals. The main PDF does not provide the necessary calculations.

The reanalysis does not state a ChatGPT model version or release year, or preregistration of its diversity outcomes. These fields are not inferred from the article date or the original experiments’ preregistrations.
notes: Only the designated extraction file was written. All of the c015 markdown was read in chunks, including its appended Reporting Summary; every page of the local PDF was read with pymupdf. Fig. 1, the reporting appendix and table detection were examined before the design checks. The six study identifiers follow the reconciled form: the paper’s wording of five experiments includes separate Experiment 2a and 2b samples. Study designs, population and tasks were independently cross-checked against the original Lee and Chung PDF at C:/Dropbox/Research/ai-lab/literature/creativity/Lee and Chung (2024) - Empirical Investigation of ChatGPT on Creativity.pdf (Methods, PDF pp. 6-8, printed pp. 1911-1913); no creativity effect from that separate paper was imported. All studies share samples with c010. Nine primary diversity-contrast records are retained even though most numerical fields are unavailable under the figure-only rule and the supplement access failure; two additional records retain the descriptive keyword counts. The single body-text Human-only percentage remains in its printed percentage units. No values were estimated from graph heights, no interval endpoints were digitized, and no statistics, rates, sample totals or effect sizes were calculated. The counts-source quotation documents secondary analysis rather than a participant count. Missing supplement results are extraction gaps, not findings of no effect. The separate Supplementary Information and its numerical claims in prior forms remain unverified in this job.
